title: MAS Guidelines on Third-Party Risk Management (proposed, 2026)
text: SYNTHETIC SUMMARY FOR POC. The proposed guidelines extend outsourcing expectations to all material third-party arrangements, require a register of third parties with criticality assessment, sub-contractor visibility to the nth party where material, documented exit strategies tested periodically, and notification to MAS before entering material arrangements involving customer information stored outside Singapore. Expected effective date: 12 months after final publication.

title: Financial data classification and grading guideline (final)
text: SYNTHETIC SUMMARY FOR POC. Financial institutions must classify data into five levels; data at level 4 and above that relates to aggregated market exposure by sector is presumed important data unless assessed otherwise. Important data may not be exported without a CAC security assessment. Institutions must maintain an important data catalogue and report it to the sector regulator annually. Effective 1 March 2027.

title: DPDP Rules 2025 - phase 2 obligations reminder
text: SYNTHETIC SUMMARY FOR POC. Data fiduciaries must notify personal data breaches to the Data Protection Board without delay and provide a detailed report within 72 hours. Consent managers obligations commence. Significant data fiduciaries must perform annual DPIA and audit. Remaining obligations phase in to 13 May 2027.

title: DORA Register of Information - ITS amendments and 2027 reporting reminder
text: SYNTHETIC SUMMARY FOR POC. Competent authorities will collect registers of information annually. Amendments clarify reporting of rank-n subcontractors supporting critical or important functions, require LEI for ICT third-party providers where available, and add a field on exit plan existence. Submission window for the 2027 reporting cycle opens 1 March 2027.

title: Client alert: AI vendor terms in financial services
text: SYNTHETIC SUMMARY FOR POC. Firms using generative AI APIs should ensure model providers are captured in third-party registers and that contracts include data-location and incident-notification clauses.
